Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for acute upper lip swelling and breathing difficulty beginning ~30 minutes after prawn soup; suspected anaphylaxis. Advised immediate 999 ambulance activation, take available antihistamine while awaiting EMS, and follow up post-hospital for epinephrine auto-injector.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Rapidly worsening upper lip swelling with breathing difficulty after eating prawn soup.
- Timeline:
  - Ate prawn soup ~7:00 PM after work.
  - Noticed left upper lip tingling/swelling ~30 minutes later; swelling progressed and now “getting bigger.”
  - During call: reported dyspnea, possible chest tightness, and dizziness.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: None reported.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Positive: Upper lip angioedema, dyspnea, dizziness; possible chest tightness.
  - Negative: No explicit report of throat closing sensation, but patient felt breathing “difficult.”
- Prior similar episode: ~1 year ago after late-night Chinese food while intoxicated; woke next morning “quite swollen” with breathing difficulty; details of trigger unknown; management at that time not recalled.
- Systems review: Limited by urgency; no further systematic review documented.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma (uses salbutamol inhaler; no other inhalers reported).
- Peanut allergy since childhood; patient reports severe reaction at ~age 6 requiring hospital care and an injection (details unknown).

Medications:
- Salbutamol inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Antihistamines “sometimes” for allergies (agent/dose/route/frequency not documented); none initially on hand during call; mother located antihistamine to take while awaiting EMS.

Allergies:
- Peanut — longstanding; reportedly severe in childhood requiring hospital visit.
- Shellfish/prawn — suspected new trigger today (not previously diagnosed).

Social History:
- Initially alone at home; mother arrived during call and remained with patient.
- Prior episode occurred after late-night meal while intoxicated.
- Tobacco, alcohol (routine use), and other substances: not documented.

Family History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- (No in-person exam; no vitals recorded.)

Investigations:
- None during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected anaphylaxis/acute allergic reaction likely triggered by prawn soup, with progressive lip angioedema, dyspnea, dizziness, and possible chest tightness; history of severe peanut allergy.
  - Plan:
    - Advised immediate emergency response: call 999 for ambulance due to suspected anaphylaxis.
    - Ensure patient not alone; mother to stay with patient until EMS arrival.
    - Take available oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.
    - Informed that hospital treatment may include an injection (epinephrine).
    - Post-hospital: patient to contact clinic for further management, including arranging epinephrine auto-injector and allergy follow-up.
- Issue 2: Asthma (background condition).
  - Plan:
    - No specific changes discussed during this urgent consult.
- Issue 3: Known peanut allergy; possible new shellfish allergy.
  - Plan:
    - Post-hospital follow-up for allergy evaluation and to “sort out injections” (epinephrine auto-injector) and management plan.

General Plan items:
- Safety net: Seek immediate emergency care for any worsening symptoms before EMS arrival.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; full review of systems; detailed physical exam; comprehensive medication list with doses/frequencies; full allergy list with reactions and severities; smoking/alcohol/substance use; family history; immunization history; prior anaphylaxis action plan; epinephrine auto-injector availability.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear overall; urgent scenario with brief, focused history; some non-linear narration and interruptions due to symptom progression.
